$comment: Full pi-smart-router.json example (four-tier policy). Copy to ~/.pi/agent/pi-smart-router.json (global) or <project>/.pi/pi-smart-router.json (project, only loaded when the project is trusted). Project config replaces global config entirely. Pi's footer keeps showing 'pi-smart-router/auto'; the [pi-smart-router] route log line identifies the actual backend used for each turn.

powerful.$comment: Expensive; reserved for genuinely difficult work and never used as a fallback.

thresholds.$comment: score <= cheapMax -> cheap tier (mimo). Trivial prompts (greetings, quick questions, one-liners) land here; cheap-code is also reachable via mechanical-task rules at any score.

escalation.$comment: Borderline-band LLM escalation: when the score lands in [minScore, maxScore] and no rule resolved the turn, the fast model re-classifies the prompt as 'fast' or 'balanced' (one tiny call, maxTokens 4, temperature 0). The classifier can never select powerful, never overrides explicit rules, and any failure (timeout, error, junk answer) keeps the heuristic tier. 'model' is optional - it defaults to the route the fast tier resolves to. Note: escalated turns send a bounded recent transcript to the classifier model (the same provider family the prompt would go to anyway).

rules.$comment: powerful (kimi-k3) only for high-confidence, genuinely difficult work. No generic keywords like 'analyze' or 'debug'.

Review requests are evaluative work (judge a diff/commit for correctness) - route to balanced even when the prompt is short and the classifier score stays low. Priority 100 'hard-*' rules still win first, so e.g. 'architecture review' goes to powerful.
cheap-code only for low-risk mechanical tasks; NOT a broad all-code rule (ordinary code prompts flow through the score tiers). With cheapMax 0 this rule is the only path to cheap-code.

$comment-fallbacks: fallbacks intentionally exclude 'powerful' - kimi-k3 must never be reached by accident.
